answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies works by binding each agent identity to a non-transferable reputation crystal grown from peer-attested interaction history. An agent that appears in a dense nebula of verified past collaborations gains weight; isolated or newly spun identities sit in the shallow ocean of low-trust scores and cannot sway consensus or claim rewards until they accumulate attested depth. Forging many cheap identities fails because each starts with zero crystal mass and must independently earn attestations that peers only grant after real cost-bearing work.
